en: Vimānavatthu:
Itthivimāna, Pīṭhavagga (The Chapter on the Stool)
15. Uttarāvimānavatthu “O goddess,
you who stand there with such exquisite beauty;”
Illuminating all directions like a star among the herbs—
by what cause is your complexion such as this?
By what means do you succeed here?
Whatever riches arise that are dear to the mind, they come to you.
I ask you, O goddess of great majesty:
while you were a human being, what merit did you perform?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing power?
"And your radiance shines in all directions.
Thus questioned by Moggallāna, that deity was uplifted in mind.
When questioned, she answered:
"This is the fruit of that karma—
envy, stinginess, and then insolence."
While living in my husband's home,
I was never angry; I lived in obedience to my husband,
always diligent in observing the Uposatha days.
On the fourteenth, the fifteenth,
and the eighth day of the fortnight,
as well as during the fortnight of miracles—
Endowed with the eight factors,
I shall observe the Uposatha,
always restrained by moral conduct.
Through self-restraint and sharing,
we dwell in a celestial mansion;
we abstain from taking life.
Restrained from false speech,
and far removed from theft, sexual misconduct,
and the drinking of intoxicants.
Delighting in the five precepts,
skilled in the Noble Truths,
these lay followers of the One with Vision—
Of the illustrious Gotama.
Thus, by my own virtue and by my fame, I too am illustrious.
I experience my own merit;
we are happy and free from illness.
Because of that, my complexion is such as this.
By that, I succeed here;
and whatever riches are dear to my mind arise for me.
I shall tell you, O monk of great power,
what I did when I was a human being; by that [deed],
I have thus become one of such blazing power.
"And my radiance shines in all directions.
And, venerable sir, with my words you should pay homage at the Blessed One's feet with your head, saying:
"Venerable sir, the female lay follower named Uttarā pays homage at the Blessed One's feet with her head."

"But it is not surprising, venerable sir, that the Blessed One should have declared me [to be established] in one of the fruits of recluseship; rather, the Blessed One has declared me [to be established] in the fruit of a once-returner.
The Fifteenth: The Vimāna of Uttarā.
